speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to help me determine the cause, can you describe exactly how you feel when the spinning occurs, such as if it is triggered by head movements or if you also feel nausea?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a classic benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) episode given the brief duration and trigger. To rule out more serious causes like a stroke or vestibular neuritis, did you notice any double vision, slurred speech, weakness in your arms or legs, or severe headache during those three minutes?
